ordinary.scope: All actual model calls retained; first attempt only, stop on first failure. Automated model time is not observed human/browser/device play duration.
limitations: Complete model-call chains are separate from sparse browser/device observations.
Reported mechanism indices remain capture-helper claims; whole-pair independent results are separate.
No game, pilot, geometry solver or future route is executed by this adapter.

independent.scope: The actual execution record retains root full source review and the complete pre-corpus static diff. Six original complete-call files were audited directly; no private diagnostics or projected replacement corpus was supplied.

mechanics.geometry: Exact integer orientation and reduced rational point markers. Proper crossing, illegal touch and positive-length overlap count unordered edge pairs; a shared graph ID excuses only its isolated common endpoint.
mechanics.validity: Conflict pairs, distinct-node coincidence, zero-length edges and integer rail validity remain separate. Guide alignment is not a victory predicate.
mechanics.rigidGroups: One canonical group position preserves every member offset; intersect all member displacement intervals and apply one uniform clamp. Blocked zero displacement costs nothing.
mechanics.controls: A selects next and B previous. Directions parallel to the selected rail request one unit. Selection is free; held inputs do not repeat.
mechanics.terminalRule: Each actual physical move first evaluates fresh geometry for success, including the last budgeted move; only then can exhausted budget lose.
mechanics.clock: Actual admitted calls and accepted dt only; no timer loss or inferred browser calls.
mechanics.ordinaryPilot: Current visible guide error chooses the next ordinary move and stops at any earlier observed win; no search, hidden route or target-position vector.

testNames: CommonJS and browser expose only create/step/config with deeply frozen public data
creation normalizes seed/level without coercion and starts fresh/unarmed
all three public starts have the exact pair counts, rational markers and rigid bounds
node/rail/segment/guide records expose actual world geometry in public order
mutable round geometry and positions do not alias config, other rounds, or segment endpoints
synthetic math: proper crossings use reduced positive-denominator rational markers
synthetic math: a shared graph endpoint alone is legal for angled or collinear segments
synthetic math: distinct-ID endpoint contact and T contact are illegal touches
synthetic math: collinear disjoint/single-point intervals and separated lines are distinguished
synthetic math: positive overlap defeats shared-ID exemption and sorts all endpoint orientations
synthetic math: all coincident pairs are ordered and zero-length omission cannot create a win
synthetic math: derivation reports fractional/out-of-range rails without clamping
parallel commands move one unit on both rail orientations; orthogonal commands are free
either selected rigid member translates the whole group and preserves the full relative vector
the shorter rail stops the entire rigid group without changing geometry or charging budget
common negative group bound and simultaneous limiting members are respected
A/B cycle a,b,c freely, including two members of the same rigid group
B rise wins simultaneous A/B/direction and every suppressed edge is consumed
A plus a fresh direction selects only and releasing A cannot replay that direction
holding A while changing direction may move without a new selection
axis clamp, strict threshold, and vertical tie use normalized held tokens
unchanged held directions never repeat; direct nonneutral changes do
new/retried state ignores held input until a genuine neutral, including bare undefined
first epoch establishes a baseline, later epoch quarantines held edges until neutral release
cancelled neutral never acknowledges release and cancelled calls still advance observations
only nonnegative safe-integer epochs are stored, and neutral epoch changes arm future calls
invalid dt is an exact no-op before descriptor reads or coercion
paused literal true is an exact no-op after complete descriptor normalization
normalization ignores inherited/getter/pulse values and accepts only literal typed own data
arrays/functions/primitives normalize wholly neutral and can arm without acting
throwing descriptors and revoked proxies atomically discard all partially read input
admitted dt advances exactly once without accumulating physics or repeating a hold
temporary ordinary terminal coincidence remains repairable and never blocks the rail move
synthetic stale caches cannot settle a no-move call or replace fresh geometry after a move
actual move receipts and replaced geometry preserve detached same-view history
current visible-guide policy wins each public task within its hand-proved cost bound
public first-group alternating policy produces three natural legal budget losses
prearranged public-input priority check wins on the real final budget move
won/lost states are exact no-ops before duration/input reads and preserve final events
synthetic counter/clock boundaries saturate only on overflow and flags remain sticky
modelTests.scope: Actual first Node spec-reporter output, retained under its original stdout.tap filename. The execution receipt records exit and five-file source window; it does not contain a command field. Synthetic math/invalid-state cases retain their explicit test labels.

checks.name: menu, version and visible canvas load
Enter starts with genuine release acknowledgement
pause freezes complete model and host tick, resume advances calls
ordinary input reaches a real win with acknowledged edges
game-specific observed rail moves and separate geometry validity conditions
measured software-browser rendering submissions stay within budget
visible retry restores the original terminal positions, selection and move budget
960 and 1280 layouts retain visible canvas and complete sidebar text
eighteen actual first-terminal moves exhaust the natural move budget
no page, console or resource errors

supplementaryControls.pointerScope: Trusted browser touch events on supplied controller assets; controlled local WebSocket transport. Actual TV response is a separately labelled host fixture.
supplementaryControls.protocolScope: Controlled public native-host input snapshots with the real shared runtime and production game. Separate from trusted controller touch transport; no physical Android/LAN/phone claim.
supplementaryControls.visualGapScope: Actual ordinary browser sessions for missing original-image coverage; declared partial stops are not terminal wins. All reads are sparse.

syntheticBlurScope.attempted: Second actual page brought to front
syntheticBlurScope.scope: Browser focus behavior only; not a physical phone or operating-system lifecycle test
syntheticBlurScope.fallback: Explicit synthetic window blur event; isTrusted false, no real-device claim

performance.note: Intervals between observer RAF callbacks on this browser; not render CPU time or device FPS. WebGL multi_draw counts API submissions, not its subdraws. Canvas paint commands are not GPU draw calls. OffscreenCanvas workers are not observed.
performance.scope: Counts are API submissions during observer RAF intervals; RAF intervals are not render CPU cost or measured television FPS.

terminalHold.scope: Conservative actual wall interval between retained read boundaries; every retained terminal model agrees. Sparse observations, not frame-exact state attribution.

cableUnweaver.finalScreenshotClockScope: last-CDP-timestamp plus measured reception-clock delta; estimated cross-clock placement
cableUnweaver.scope: All state readStartedAt/readCompletedAt fields bound real awaited reads; browser observations remain sparse.

invocationHistory.scope: First actual capture and first encoding succeeded. Original encoder stderr retains its deprecated JPEG pixel-format warning; explicit full-to-TV range conversion was requested. Full decoder and verifier stderr are empty.
